TWO DECISIONS AN OPERATOR MUST SETTLE BEFORE AN UNATTENDED BUILDER STARTS — this is why autonomousSafe is false, not a decline:
(1) THE FEAT'S OWN PERF AC IS UNACHIEVABLE AS WRITTEN. It asks for 'p95 render under 150 ms on the 120k store' while excluding new indexes/migrations. No index on memories leads with created_at (verified over all of migrations/: the full set is idx_memories_agent, _archival_candidates, _capture_source, _consent_disclosed, _repo_type, _session, _speaker_label, _purge_batch, _project_valid_created, _needs_vec_index, _evidence_turn), so ORDER BY created_at DESC plus a filtered COUNT are unindexed scans of 120k rows, and the profile filter's correlated transcripts subquery (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:276-290) must be evaluated per candidate row for the COUNT. Independently, the whole page already cold-renders in ~7.9s at 16k memories (documented at src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:628-633), so a 150 ms WHOLE-RENDER budget fails on arrival regardless of this change. AC-5 restates it as a feed-query-scoped budget with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN evidence and an explicit FAIL-with-evidence path; confirm that restatement or lift the index exclusion.
(2) JOB-ROW SEMANTICS CHANGE OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR. Today buildActivityRows merges up to 10 queryRecentFailedJobs rows (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:412) into the memory pool and sorts by timestamp, so a job row can legitimately land on page 2. The FEAT's 'job-failure rows only on page 1' pins them instead, which shifts every memory offset on page 1 and makes 'of Z' ambiguous (memories only, or memories plus jobs?). AC-7 resolves it as: jobs on page 1 only, Z counts memories, job count stated separately. Confirm or override.

risks: PRE-MORTEM Q1 (most likely review/validation failure in two weeks): an off-by-one between the SQL OFFSET and the caption. offset = (page-1)*15 must agree with 'showing 736-750 of 1180' at page 50 and with totalPages = ceil(1180/15) = 79. The clamp currently derives its total from rows.length inside the renderer (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:527, :537, :570), so the moment the total comes from a separate COUNT the two can disagree silently — nothing fails loudly, the operator just sees a wrong caption or a skipped row at each page boundary.

PRE-MORTEM Q2 (merged and broke the daemon — what does rollback actually require): git revert only. Two source files plus two test files, no migration, no schema or wire-contract change, no published artifact. The blast radius that is NOT revert-cheap is operational: better-sqlite3 is synchronous, so an unindexed COUNT added to the render path blocks the event loop and starves /health, which is the exact 2026-07-13 wedge-then-watchdog-kill restart loop documented at src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:628-645. A bad merge degrades the whole daemon, not just /dashboard — which is what AC-6's slow-query log and AC-5's isolated measurement exist to catch before that.

PRE-MORTEM Q3 (which existing test would NOT catch a regression): none of the five pagination tests at tests/server/dashboard-html.test.ts:264-312 would. Every one builds recentMemories as a 20-element JS array via manyMemories() and asserts on renderDashboard output, so a wrong LIMIT, a wrong OFFSET, a wrong COUNT WHERE clause, or a count/page disagreement all stay green. The only DB-backed coverage is tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts:232-376, which never asserts anything about row counts or windows. AC-8 closes exactly this gap.

REPEAT-LESSON RISK, quoted from the direct predecessor's grade (.claude/artifacts/loop/grades/20261106T033206Z-feat554-slice448-grade.md): 'A real functional bug shipped past unit tests and the first self-review... 84/84 green tests gave false confidence; the defect was only found once something reproduced the actual two-field submission'. The same failure shape is available here: fixture-level pagination tests pass while the real SQL window is wrong. That slice graded test_confidence 0.55 and reliability 0.60 after two fix rounds. The verifier must drive a real DB at two different offsets, not a fixture array.

PERF LANDMINE, established by inspection not by benchmark: the profile filter is the worst case. Its correlated subquery against transcripts (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:276-290) is evaluated per candidate row, and a filtered COUNT(*) has no LIMIT to stop it early, so ?profile=X on a 120k store becomes an unbounded per-row subquery scan. The existing LIMIT 25 masks this today by stopping after 25 matches. This is the single most likely way the slice misses AC-5 while agent-only and project-only filters pass.

SCOPE-CONTRADICTION RISK: the FEAT excludes new indexes while demanding a 150 ms budget that likely needs one (see scopeNotes decision 1). An unattended builder facing this either fabricates the perf evidence or silently adds a migration outside stated scope. Both are worse than a FAIL with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output, which is what AC-5 mandates.

INJECTION CHECK: none found. The FEAT-555 body (.claude/artifacts/loop/backlog/pending/FEAT-555.md) contains no embedded imperative attempting to steer scoring, priority or autonomous_safe; it is an ordinary scope/acceptance description. Nothing to quote.

acs: AC-1: Given a store where memories.agent = 'crew:reviewer' matches 1,180 of ~120,000 rows, When an operator requests /dashboard?agent=crew:reviewer&page=50, Then queryRecentMemories (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:263) returns exactly the 15 rows at SQL offset 735 ordered created_at DESC, and renderActivityPager (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:537) renders the caption 'page 50/79 - showing 736-750 of 1180' with both a working prev and a working next anchor.

AC-2: Given the MemoryListFilters WHERE composition inside queryRecentMemories (the conditions/params arrays at src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:264-300, covering project equality, project IS NULL, the transcripts correlated-subquery profile clause, profile IS NULL, agent equality and agent IS NULL), When the new total-count query is built, Then it consumes that same single composition extracted to one shared helper rather than a second hand-written WHERE, and a test asserts the count equals the number of rows the page query can reach for every filter shape already pinned in tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts:232-376.

AC-3: Given an agent filter value matching no stored row - the ?agent=does-not-exist-anywhere case already pinned for the row query at tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts:370 - When /dashboard renders with that filter, Then the total count is 0, the caption reads 'page 1/1', renderActivityPager emits no prev or next anchor (it returns the empty string at total === 0), the response status is 200, and the feed shows its empty-state text rather than falling back to the unfiltered set.

AC-4: Given a filtered history of 1,180 matching rows (79 pages at 15 per page), When ?page= is supplied as '0', 'abc', '-5' or '999999', Then resolveActivityPage (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:527) clamps to 1, 1, 1 and 79 respectively, and the rows actually rendered are the rows at that clamped page's SQL offset - asserted against a real DB fixture built with the insertMemory helper (tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts:224), not a baseData({ recentMemories }) in-memory array.

AC-5: Given a seeded store of 120,000 memories rows, When the two activity-feed statements (the filtered page query and the filtered total-count query) are timed in isolation over 20 runs for ?agent=crew:reviewer&page=50, Then their combined p95 is under 150 ms and the validation artifact records both the measured p95 and the EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output for each statement. Given the budget is missed, When the cause is a missing index, Then the slice reports FAIL with that evidence and stops - it must not add an index or migration, which the FEAT body places out of scope, and it must not quietly restate the budget against the whole-page render, which already cold-renders in ~7.9s at 16k memories (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:628-633).

AC-6: Given the activity-feed page query or total-count query executes during a GET /dashboard, When either statement's elapsed time exceeds 250 ms, Then a single structured warn event is emitted through the logger already imported at src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:11, carrying the active filter keys, the resolved page, the SQL offset and the elapsed milliseconds - so a recurrence of the 2026-07-13 synchronous-render wedge (src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:628-645) is visible in logs instead of inferred from a dead /health.

AC-7: Given no memory filter is active (isMemoryFilterActive returns false, src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:369) and queryRecentFailedJobs returns up to 10 rows (src/server/queries/dashboard.ts:412), When the feed renders, Then those job rows appear above the memory rows on page 1 only, pages 2 and later contain memory rows exclusively, and the caption's Z counts memories alone with the job-row count stated separately. Given any project, profile or agent filter IS active, When any page renders, Then no job row appears on it - preserving the existing carve-out documented at src/server/routes/dashboard-html.ts:476-480.

AC-8: Given the five existing pagination tests at tests/server/dashboard-html.test.ts:264-312 construct recentMemories as 20-element in-memory fixtures and exercise no SQL (their own comment reads 'in-memory slice over the already-fetched rows (no new SQL)'), When paging moves into queryRecentMemories, Then at least one new DB-backed test inserts more than 30 rows via insertMemory (tests/server/queries/dashboard-queries.test.ts:224), calls the query at page 1 and page 3, and asserts the two returned id sets are disjoint and jointly ordered created_at DESC; and the untouched filter deep-link assertions at tests/server/dashboard-html.test.ts:470 and :543 still pass.
